'''Wendell Earl Dunn Jr.''' (August 30, 1922&nbsp;– December 24, 2007) was an American [[chemical engineer]], [[metallurgy|metallurgist]], and inventor. His technologies for high temperature [[chlorination reaction|chlorination]], gold, tantalum and titanium extraction are still widely used.{{citation needed|date=August 2018}}

==Early years==
Dunn was the first son of educator [[Wendell E. Dunn]], for many years principal of [[Forest Park High School (Maryland)|Forest Park High School]] in Baltimore, and brother of conductor [[Thomas Dunn (musician)|Thomas Dunn]]. A graduate of [[Baltimore City College]] and [[Johns Hopkins University]], Dunn was also awarded a [[doctorate]] in chemical engineering from Johns Hopkins. After completing the Harvard/MIT [[V-12 Navy College Training Program|V-12 program]] in 1944, he was engaged in aircraft terrain avoidance [[radar]] research in both the U.S. and [[occupied Germany]]. Dunn served as [[Captain (United States)|captain]] in the [[U.S. Army Air Corps]] until 1946.

==Chemical research==
[[Image:Wdunnmorgan.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Wendell Dunn at pilot plant for producing low-cost titanium process feedstock, [[Mount Morgan, Queensland]], Australia, ca 1975.]]
In 1950 Dunn was a key member of the research and development team at [[DuPont|E.I. DuPont de Nemours]] in [[Wilmington, Delaware]] which developed an improved process for the production of high-purity [[titanium dioxide]] for use as a paint pigment. He filed his first sole-inventor U.S. patent in 1954.<ref>Charging fluidizing gas into fluidized bed reactor. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr, US Patent number: 2856264 Filed Apr 9, 1954 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US2856264]</ref> He remained with the firm for 19 years during which time this process grew to become the dominant technology worldwide.

In 1968 Dunn left DuPont to form his own contract research and development firm in Delaware and [[Sydney]], Australia. He worked closely for several years with a major Australian mining house, [[Peko-Wallsend]], to develop a technology to produce a low-cost titanium process feedstock.<ref>Process for beneficiation of titaniferous ores. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr, US Patent number: 3699206 Filing date: Mar 23, 1970 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US3699206]</ref><ref>Process for preparing alkali-metal tetrachloroferrate. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. US Patent number: 3729543 Filing date: Jan 21, 1971 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US3729543]</ref>
Thereafter, Dunn returned to [[South Dakota]] and for the next three decades made significant contributions to the field of high-temperature chlorination of metal ores.<ref>Wendell E. Dunn. High temperature chlorination of titanium bearing minerals: part III. Metallurgical and Materials Transactions B. Volume 10, Number 2 / June, 1979. Pages 293–294 [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02652473]</ref><ref>Wendell E. Dunn. High temperature chlorination of titanium bearing minerals: part IV. Metallurgical and Materials Transactions B. Volume 10, Number 2 / June, 1979. Pages 271–277 [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02652471]</ref><ref>Process for beneficiating titaniferous ores. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. US Patent number: 4389391 Filing date: Jun 28, 1981 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US4389391]</ref><ref>Process for beneficiating a titaniferous ore and production of chlorine and iron oxide. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. US Patent number: 3865920, Filing date: Mar 14, 1973 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US3865920]</ref><ref name="JPC">{{cite journal |last1=Cook |first1=Charles M. |last2=Dunn |first2=Wendell E. |title=The Reaction of Ferric Chloride with Sodium and Potassium Chlorides |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry |date=September 1961 |volume=65 |issue=9 |pages=1505–1511 |doi=10.1021/j100905a008 }}</ref>

Between 1975 and 1995 Dunn consulted to international corporations [[Reynolds Metals]],<ref>Alumina from alkali metal-aluminum chloride complexes. US Patent number: 4331645 Filing date: Apr 20, 1981 Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. [https://patents.google.com/patent/US4331645]</ref> [[Kerr-McGee]] and DuPont, among others and performed R&D which formed the bases for several start-up ventures in South Dakota and beyond. He worked with the [[Lien Brothers]] and others in the [[Rapid City]] area to develop processes for the extraction of ultra-pure [[niobium]] from ore,<ref>Process for the production of niobium pentachloride. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. US Patent number: 3153572.
Filing date: Jun 1, 1961 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US3153572]
</ref> and tantalum metals for use in electronic applications, and for the efficient separation and recovery of gold from low-grade ore and scrap.<ref>Chlorine extraction of gold. Inventor: Wendell E. Dunn, Jr. Patent number: 4353740
Filing date: Sep 11, 1981 [https://patents.google.com/patent/US4353740]</ref><ref>Dunn, Wendell. Chlorine extraction of gold – Chapter 10. in Gold, Silver, Uranium, and Coal: Geology, Mining, Extraction & Environment. Maurice C. Fuerstenau, Bruce R. Palmer. American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers, Black Hills Section. American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers, 1983.[https://books.google.com/books?id=zNS3AAAACAAJ&q=Gold,+Silver,+Uranium,+And+Coal+Geology,+Mining,+Extraction+And+The+Environment]</ref>

From the late-1980s until the late-1990s Dunn joined with European and Asian interests to develop a process for low-cost titanium-based pigments, and worked in India for months at a time. He was an adjunct faculty member in metallurgy at the [[South Dakota School of Mines and Technology]], and was working on a patent application at the time of his death.<ref>Cyclical vacuum chlorination processes, including lithium extraction. US Patent Application 20050220691 Filed: March 28, 2005 [http://appft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&co1=AND&d=PG01&s1=wendell.IN.&s2=dunn.IN.&OS=IN/wendell+AND+IN/dunn&RS=IN/wendell+AND+IN/dunn]</ref>

Dunn had a whimsical side, and in 1979 penned a political satire, ''The Sex Tax.''<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=Bctto8NtPoUC ''The Sex Tax'' on Google Books]</ref><ref>[http://sites.google.com/site/thesextaxsite ''The Sex Tax'' complete text]</ref> Dunn is interred in [[Green Mount Cemetery]] in Baltimore. He was the nephew of civil engineer [[Everett Dunn]].{{citation needed |date=May 2026}}
